title: Kale, frozen, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Kale is a leafy cruciferous vegetable known for its high levels of vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants. This product is frozen, pre‑cooked without added fat, and ready to use in dishes without further cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kale is often called a “superfood” because of its dense nutrient profile.
Freezing preserves most of its vitamins, especially vitamin C and carotenoids.
Kale is a close relative of broccoli, Brussels sprouts, and cabbage.
In the wild, kale grows in coastal regions of Europe and Asia, tolerating strong winds.
Its fiber content is higher than that of most leafy greens.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Kale provides over 500 % of the daily value for vitamin K, which is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and enhances iron absorption.

items.title: High in antioxidants
items.content: Kale contains polyphenols and carotenoids that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Mineral dense
items.content: It supplies calcium, magnesium, and iron, nutrients important for bones, muscles, and blood formation.

items.title: Low‑calorie protein and fiber source
items.content: Kale offers plant protein and dietary fiber, promoting satiety and healthy digestion.

items.title: Possible interaction with blood thinners
items.content: The high vitamin K content may reduce the effectiveness of anticoagulant medications.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Kale contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience an allergy to cruciferous vegetables.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Frozen cooked kale can be added to soups, stews, smoothies, salads, or used as a side dish. It reheats quickly in the microwave or a skillet without added oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep kale in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After thawing, use within 2–3 days and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
